agents.label: Media librarian
responsibilities: import asset metadata
create thumbnails
index filenames
manage local asset IDs
persist local project references
cannot: infer semantic contents beyond file metadata
claim visual understanding
upload original media to a model provider
send resized previews without explicit consent

agents.label: Online asset scout
responsibilities: search Wikimedia Commons and normalize source and licence metadata
search optional Pexels endpoints only with a configured server-side key
download selected supported media from allowlisted official HTTPS hosts under a 24 MB cap
open Pinterest search links as reference research without scraping or auto-downloading Pins
cannot: claim visual relevance from titles or descriptions alone
treat missing licence metadata as verified reuse permission
crawl arbitrary websites or download from unapproved hosts
bypass platform access controls or scrape Pinterest
limitations: Never invoke this role from the default prompt-to-video workflow; video scenes must be authored and rendered with code.

agents.label: Visual search query planner
responsibilities: remove production-instruction noise from a visual brief
produce multiple concise subject/action/object query variants
prioritise the most specific query and broader concept phrases
return attempted-query metadata so poor search can be diagnosed
limitations: this is deterministic phrase decomposition, not an LLM semantic planner
it does not visually inspect results or guarantee semantic relevance
Google Images remains reference-link based for new API customers
Pinterest remains reference-link only until OAuth and approved API access exist
Not part of default prompt-to-video; the default creation path must not formulate asset-search queries.
release_gate: query-variant tests for action prompts and science prompts
deduplication across provider searches
honest search query reporting
eventual scene-level search plans from the shared production manifest

agents.label: Timeline executor
responsibilities: apply deterministic shot settings
compose text overlays
apply supported pan and zoom presets
record a local WebM draft
run the code-first render and require actual encoded-file technical QA before import
route human briefs to the procedural Three.js code renderer
require rendered-frame visual review before artistic approval
cannot: edit original source files destructively
claim support for unimplemented effects
silently use paid compute
use online assets or generated still images as a substitute for code-authored video scenes
mark a render as visually approved without a frame-level visual critique
claim the procedural 3D character is photorealistic without evidence

agents.label: Visual analyst
agents.input_policy: user-consented selected assets or generated low-resolution frames only
responsibilities: describe composition and likely shot content from explicitly selected resized previews
compare a selected batch of shot previews with the director brief
report visible evidence and uncertainty without claiming to inspect full video clips
release_gate: configured provider route and actual worker/model identity
explicit consent before each remote preview-analysis request
asset-ID grounding and JPEG payload-bound tests
provider timeout, quota, incomplete-result and malformed-plan tests

agents.label: Creative director
responsibilities: convert the brief and selected preview evidence into a structured proposed edit plan
suggest bounded per-shot timing, supported motion, framing and text-overlay changes
emit a schema-validated plan bound to actual local clip and asset IDs
release_gate: manual review or explicit per-run consent before automatic timeline mutation
fresh-timeline validation before apply
post-render visual critique before claiming end-to-end autonomous quality
benchmark suite across distinct visual tasks

agents.label: Graphics and motion engineer
agents.execution_mode: Shared, consent-gated creative-director model call; not a separately deployed model or independent second opinion.
responsibilities: propose editable typography and explanatory text overlays
construct native rectangles, circles, lines and arrows with bounded opacity and geometry
select restrained fade/slide/scale entry motion only when it serves an explanatory purpose
follow strict anti-slop constraints and use schema-validated native layer data
cannot: inject scripts, HTML, SVG or arbitrary code into the renderer
claim generated raster imagery, keyframes or transitions that are not implemented
stack more than three added graphic layers on one shot
use decorative particles, fake HUDs, glows, filler labels or motion without a communication purpose
release_gate: schema and coordinate bounds tested
explicit consent before sending resized previews
per-run auto-apply consent or manual review before application
post-render visual critique remains a separate unmet release gate

agents.label: Motion-graphics engineer
responsibilities: propose purposeful shot pacing and supported motion presets
map graphic hierarchy and motion intent to validated timeline operations
avoid decorative motion that does not explain or direct attention
prefer clear visual cause-and-effect and readable timing over effects for their own sake
cannot: claim to be a separate deployed model or independent second opinion
create unsupported keyframes, transitions, audio tracks or effects
claim AI-directed edits unless the configured model call returned and validated a proposal
guarantee professional quality without inspecting the rendered result
release_gate: editable layer data
design-system constraints
rendered-frame inspection
safe rollback
honest provider identity and error reporting
agents.execution_mode: Shared, consent-gated role within the existing creative-director model call. It is not an independently deployed specialist model. The browser Canvas renderer performs the actual supported animation and WebM recording.

agents.label: Visual critic
responsibilities: inspect up to four midpoint frames decoded from the actual first exported WebM
compare visible output composition with the brief
identify concrete, frame-supported issues such as irrelevant shots, text obstruction or bad crops
propose only schema-validated corrections and allow one bounded correction/re-render pass
release_gate: real rendered-frame input from a decodable WebM
explicit per-run consent before frame egress
bounded correction count and fresh-timeline validation
technical QA of final re-render
independent-critic benchmark remains future work
agents.execution_mode: Consent-gated post-render prompt sent through the existing creative-director provider; not a separately deployed model or independent second opinion.
cannot: claim to inspect audio, motion between sampled frames or unseen portions of source clips
independently validate the model that produced the edit
perform a second AI critique of the corrected final render
guarantee visual quality or eliminate every form of AI slop

agents.label: Manim scientific renderer
responsibilities: render validated scientific and mathematical node-arrow diagrams to MP4
accept artifact labels and bounded coordinates rather than arbitrary source code
return an explicit unavailable result when Manim is not installed
report render timeout, output path, output size and technical failure honestly
cannot: execute model-written Python
claim to be available until the host executable is present
replace assets owned by another renderer without an explicit task assignment
claim the MP4 has passed visual or scientific review merely because it rendered
release_gate: Manim executable/version probe on the actual deployed host
representative scene render and MP4 decode validation
container CPU/memory/process limits
artifact persistence and Studio timeline import
visual inspection of final rendered output

agents.label: Code-first video renderer
responsibilities: construct original scenes procedurally in code
animate scene state over time and render a complete encoded video
reopen the encoded file and verify decoding, dimensions, duration, blank frames and meaningful motion
request visual critique of rendered frames only with explicit per-run consent
label technical drafts as unapproved until visual critique succeeds
cannot: search for or download images/assets during prompt-to-video
generate still images as a substitute for motion
pass off a stick/line/circle figure as a believable human
claim artistic approval from technical checks alone
release_gate: code-only prompt-to-video regression tests
human/animal low-fidelity quality gate
rendered-frame visual review and bounded correction
on-device render/export playback tests

agents.label: Code Rendering Engineer
responsibilities: translate a brief into a deterministic scene graph, geometry, materials, lighting, camera and time-based animation using code
prefer coherent anatomical volumes, articulated joints, face landmarks, hands and grounded contact over stick figures or primitive placeholders
render an actual encoded video and validate dimensions, duration, decodability and nonblank frames
use the actual rendered frames as evidence; make bounded code corrections when a visual critic identifies concrete defects
state renderer limits honestly and fail closed for unsupported subjects
cannot: search for or download images as a substitute for code-authored scenes
generate a still image and present it as the requested video
claim photorealism without rendered-frame evidence
call technical decode checks proof of artistic quality
add decorative particles, meaningless HUDs, filler text, or geometry without a communication purpose
engineering_contract: implement a measurable feature, not only a prompt change
add regression tests for subject routing and output validity
handle timeouts and dispose GPU/media resources
separate technical QA from artistic approval
never mark a feature production-ready until browser/device rendering is tested

coordination_contract.rule: Specialist labels must not imply independent execution. The target runtime uses one shared production manifest with stable artifact IDs, scoped ownership, dependency edges, and a task ledger.
